newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends easy, gilts down on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: India call ends easy, gilts down on profit taking.

text.p: Indian call money ended Thursday easier at 5.50-5.75 percent against the opening 6.0-6.75 percent, dealers said.
"There were some trades in the morning at 6.50-6.75 percent but rates eased to 5.5-6.0 percent within half an hour," said a dealer.
He said though Thursday's rates were higher than Wednesday's rates, liquidity remained good within the banking system.
Call money ended Wednesday at 3.0-3.5 percent but opened higher on Thursday on account of funds outflow.
The Reserve Bank of India mopped up 30.35 billion rupees at a four-day auction of government of India securities on Wednesday, with payments by successful bidders to be made on Thursday.
Dealers said the ouflow pushed rates up.
"Basically, the repos rate of 5.0 percent is evolving as a kind of benchmark for call money rates," a dealer said.
Prices of government securities fell in thin trade on Thursday as higher call rates affected sentiment and led to profit-taking, dealers said.
Traded volumes on the National Stock Exchange fell to 1.50 billion rupees from Wednesay's 2.01 billion, dealers said.

The 13.40 percent government of India 1999 stock fell to 101.98 rupees from 102.05, the 13.50 percent 1997 stock to 101.58 from 101.67 rupees, and the 13.50 percent 1998 stock to 103.20 from 103.27, a dealer said.
He said yields on tresury bills maturing in July 1997 rose ten basis points to 9.35 percent, while the April 1997 maturity treasury bills rose 15 basis points to 7.85 percent.
Banks are closed on Friday for a local holiday and reopen on Saturday.
